To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of gallium nitride (GaN)-based power electronics can achieve significant mass savings in DC generation applications.
the application of Gallium Nitride devices can improve the efficiency and reduce the mass of a DC generation system.
the application of Gallium Nitride devices in power conversion systems can lead to a significant mass savings relative to SiC and Si devices at the same level of system loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multi-objective optimization framework that can be utilized to predict Pareto-optimal solutions for power conversion systems.
the development and implementation of a rigorous design methodology that enables the design of power conversion systems with the best performance for a given set of constraints.
the design optimization of a power converter system with a GaN device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of a GaN device in a DC generation system can improve the Pareto-optimum performance of the converter design.
GaN devices have a great potential for power conversion applications.
the application of the GaN technology in the design of a power conversion system can result in a significant reduction of mass and volume, and thus a reduction in cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GaN devices can achieve a 40% mass saving over Si at the same loss, and a 6.5% mass savings over SiC at the same loss.
the application of the proposed design paradigm and the GaN devices can enable significant mass savings and thus improve system performance.

GaN devices are a good choice for applications that have high switching frequency requirements, high power density requirements, high junction temperature rating requirements, or a combination of the above.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of multi-objective optimization can help identify and quantify the Pareto-optimum design space and thus enable better informed decisions for power converter designs.
a multi-objective optimization paradigm is essential to predict and understand the trade-offs between performance, cost, and mass for the design of a power conversion system with GaN devices.

the use of GaN devices can lead to significant improvements in power converter performance and thus enable the design of lighter and more efficient power converters for aerospace and other power electronic applications.
